title: Real-time telemetry smithy: kernel curator with per-flow safety & warmstart
creator: Lena Chen
description: Goal: Build a low-overhead, real-time kernel curator (codename: Smithy) that uses short online micro-experiments driven by per-request telemetry to pick the best attention and matmul kernels for mixed prefill/decode workloads. The curator must: (1) respect customer latency SLOs (including tail), (2) warmstart from an offline fingerprint reservoir to avoid cold exploration, (3) safely hedge with fast fallbacks when risk of regression is detected, and (4) produce per-customer and per-model kernel recommendations that account for architecture (A100/RTX/GPU types), sequence-length distribution, and decode ratio (prefill-heavy vs streaming decode).
acceptance_criteria:
1) Smithy runs in hosted and Dedicated modes with <2% added p99 latency under normal traffic.
2) For 80% of customer flows we get >=5% cost improvement vs baseline kernel assignment without increasing error/regression alerts.
3) Rollout mechanism supports canary on 5% traffic, automatic rollback when p99 latency increases >5ms or error-rate increases >0.2%.
4) Warmstart uses offline fingerprint bank; if fingerprint match score >0.78 we avoid exploration and apply recommended kernel immediately.
risks_and_mitigation:
- Risk: Exploration probes could increase tail latency. Mitigation: use ultra-lightweight microbench probes (single-request shadowing) and run expensive trials only during low-load windows; always maintain a fast fallback kernel and circuit-breaker thresholds.
- Risk: Fingerprint collisions across customers could misrecommend kernels. Mitigation: add per-customer weighting and require repeated confirmation before committing a new policy.
- Risk: Hardware heterogeneity (chiplet / MIG / memory fragmentation). Mitigation: tag telemetry with node topology and enforce architecture compatibility gating for kernel variants.
implementation_notes:
Design: profiler collects a compact fingerprint: (avg_seq, median_seq, decode_ratio, token_phase_entropy, peak_batch_size, kv_cache_hit_rate, recent_latency_p95). Smithy ranks candidate kernels via a multi-objective score combining latency estimate, token-cost estimate, and risk score (based on stable delta from warmstart). Online optimizer: short-lived Bayesian bandit with safe-constraint (do not exceed p95 budget) and warmstart priors from offline cost surface.
Telemetry pipeline: extend /metrics/kernel_probe to include microprobe results and add a dashboard slice for smithy decisions. Prefill/decode interplay: add logic to bias kernel selection towards prefill-optimized kernels for sequences with decode_ratio < 0.2 and vice versa for streaming chat.
APIs: expose smithy.get_suggestion(model, fingerprint) and smithy.report_observation(decision_id, latency, success). Decisions should be idempotent and annotated for audit logs.
work_items: instrument lightweight microprobe in runtime (prefill path)
create constrained Bayesian bandit module with safety checks
comments: 2025-02-10 Lena Chen: Initial PRD posted to Confluence (see links). We propose Smithy as an opt-in runtime module for a staged canary. Core constraint: zero regressions on customer-visible p99. Keeping estimate conservative (5 points).

2025-02-12 Marco Delgado: Reviewed the scoring function. Suggested adding token_phase_entropy to fingerprint to better capture prefills with long trailing priming. Also proposed fast-path caching for high-frequency flows.

2025-02-14 Owen Brooks: Prototype of microprobe integrated; end-to-end microprobe adds ~0.5ms median overhead when sampled at 0.5% traffic. Running nightly offline replay to validate. Found one corner case where decode-heavy bursts trigger fallback too often; adjusting decay window from 30s->120s.

2025-02-16 Riley Park (Performance): Ran cluster stress. With warmstart enabled, Smithy matched offline best-kernel in 72% of flows within first 10 minutes; without warmstart it took >1 hour. We should prioritize warmstart reservoir ingestion. Attached sample CSV to links.

2025-02-18 Security Review (Anita Rao): No secrets in telemetry; need to ensure fingerprint hash is non-reversible and does not include raw prompts. Marking security_review_required=true and adding KMS field to audit logs.
